web_evidence.title: Extreme Prey - Preview
web_evidence.note: The author's authorized preview supplies Chapters One through Three in sustained third-person narration, shifting focalization among Marlys, Cole, Lucas, Kidd, and Elle without a participating narrator.

web_evidence.title: Extreme Prey
web_evidence.note: The full-book review describes parallel access to Lucas's investigation and the Purdys' plot, including information known to the reader but not Lucas, corroborating the external multi-focal structure shown by the prose.

web_evidence.title: Extreme Prey
web_evidence.note: The review states that the book reveals Marlys and Cole's plans from the opening and follows Lucas toward the resolution, corroborating the two externally narrated plot strands.

search_log: Searched "Extreme Prey" "John Sandford" with excerpt, first chapter, and third-person terms; located the publisher listing and a Bookreporter excerpt.
Opened Penguin Random House's title page; it verified the edition and offered a sample but its rendered page exposed only catalog copy, not sample prose.
Searched the author's official site and opened its authorized Preview Chapters page, which supplied sustained prose from Chapters One through Three.
Opened Bookreporter's excerpt and full review; the excerpt duplicated the authorized opening, while the review described the book-wide reader/Lucas information split.
Searched Google Books/Google Play and library/OverDrive records; accessible pages offered catalog descriptions or audio samples rather than diagnostic prose.

Ran targeted searches for point of view, third-person, narrator perspective, multiple viewpoints, epistolary form, and alternating narration; no credible source indicated first-person, second-person, epistolary, or alternating-person sections.
Opened Publishers Weekly's review, which corroborated that the novel exposes the plotters' plans while following Lucas's investigation but did not explicitly name the grammatical POV.
person_note: The controlling narration is third person. The authorized opening sustains external narration across several focal characters, and the sampled interior scenes and epilogue continue the same pattern through Lucas, Marlys, Cole, and others. First- and second-person forms in the quotes are dialogue or generic free-indirect 'you,' not autonomous narrating sections. The main limitation is that the authorized web excerpt covers only the first three chapters, but numerous interior and end-of-book quotes independently corroborate third person, while whole-book reviews describe the same parallel plotter/investigator structure and targeted searches found no contrary or alternating-person evidence.
